articles._summary: U.S. stock futures were mixed on Friday, mirroring the moves on Thursday, with the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 indexes declining, while futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) edged up. articles.headline: Micron Stock Takes A Breather After Explosive AI-Fueled Rally
articles.summary: Micron (MU) stock dips 5% premarket after a massive 15% rally. Investors lock in profits despite a stellar, AI-driven earnings beat.
articles._summary: Micron reported adjusted earnings per share of $25.11 on revenue of $41.46 billion, while adjusted gross margin reached 84.9%. The company also forecast fiscal fourth-quarter adjusted EPS of about $31 on revenue of roughly $50 billion. Management said it has signed multi-year strategic customer agreements designed to make revenue and earnings more predictable. Analysts also pointed to sustained pricing strength for AI-focused DRAM and NAND memory as another positive sign for the business.

articles.headline: Mohamed El-Erian Says Gold Needs One Key Buyer To Break Out Of Its $4,000 Slump
articles.summary: El-Erian believes central bank buying could lift gold out of its slump. Lower oil prices could support this trend.
articles._summary: Economist Mohamed El-Erian on Thursday said that the renewed buying by central banks could lift gold out of its recent slump after the precious metal briefly fell below $4,000 an ounce this week. In a post on X, El-Erian said the biggest factor that could reverse gold’s recent weakness is “renewed, consistent central bank buying.” He added that lower oil prices could support that trend by easing pressure on many countries’ foreign exchange reserves, potentially allowing central banks to resume accumulating gold.

articles._zh_summary: 经济学家Mohamed El-Erian周四表示，在金价本周短暂跌破4,000美元/盎司之后，央行重新买盘可能会使金价摆脱近期的暴跌。 El-Erian 在 X 上发表的一篇文章中表示，扭转黄金近期疲软趋势的最大因素是“央行重新持续购买”。他补充说，油价下跌可能会缓解许多国家外汇储备的压力，从而支持这一趋势，从而有可能让各国央行恢复积累黄金。

articles.headline: Rescuers search rubble for survivors as Venezuela earthquakes kill at least 235
articles.summary: At least 4,300 people have been injured after two seven-plus magnitude shallow quakes hit seconds apart.
articles._summary: Rescues and prayers a day after Venezuelan earthquakes Rescuers are searching through rubble in a rush to save lives after two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela near the capital, killing at least 235 people and injuring at least 4,300. In Caracas and the nearby coastal city of La Guaira, people could be heard calling for help from under the debris of collapsed buildings. The first 7.2-magnitude quake was followed seconds later by an even stronger 7.5-magnitude one, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS), with both occurring close to the surface, making destruction more severe. Many more people are feared dead, with others left homeless or too afraid to stay in damaged, unsafe buildings sleeping in the streets after the disaster. The earthquakes struck at 18:04 local time (22:04 GMT) on Wednesday - a national holiday in Venezuela, meaning more people would have been at home than on a normal weekday.
articles._zh_headline: 委内瑞拉地震造成至少 235 人死亡，救援人员在废墟中搜寻幸存者
articles._zh_summary: 委内瑞拉地震发生一天后的救援和祈祷 委内瑞拉首都附近发生两次强烈地震，造成至少 235 人死亡、至少 4,300 人受伤，救援人员正在废墟中搜寻，急于拯救生命。在加拉加斯和附近的沿海城市拉瓜伊拉，可以听到人们在倒塌建筑物的废墟下呼救。据美国地质调查局 (USGS) 称，第一次 7.2 级地震几秒钟后又发生了更强烈的 7.5 级地震，两次地震都发生在靠近地表的地方，造成破坏更加严重。灾难发生后，人们担心会有更多的人死亡，还有一些人无家可归，或者不敢住在受损、不安全的建筑里，睡在街上。地震发生在当地时间周三 18:04（格林威治标准时间 22:04），当时恰逢委内瑞拉的国定假日，这意味着在家中的人数比正常工作日要多。
